source_text: Porro consequens erat, ut cui demandabat evangelii administrationem non passim nec inconsiderate administrandam, adiceret secundum dominicam vocem, ne margaritam porcis et sanctum canibus iactaret. Dominus palam edixit, sine ulla significatione alicuius tecti sacramenti. Ipse praeceperat, si quid in tenebris et in abscondito audissent, in luce et in tectis praedicarent. Ipse per similitudinem praefiguraverat, ne unam mnam, id est unum verbum eius, sine fructu in abdito reservarent. Ipse docebat lucernam non sub modium abstrudi solere, sed in candelabrum constitui, ut luceat omnibus qui in domo sunt. Haec apostoli aut neglexerunt aut minime intellexerunt, si non adimpleverunt, abscondentes aliquid de Lumine, id est de dei verbo et Christi sacramento. Neminem, quod scio, verebantur, non Iudaeorum vim, non ethnicorum; quo magis utique in ecclesia libere praedicabant qui in synagogis et in locis publicis non tacebant. Immo neque Iudaeos convertere neque ethnicos inducere potuissent, nisi quod credi ab eis volebant ordine exponerent. Multo magis iam credentibus ecclesiis nihil subtraxissent quod aliis paucis seorsum demandarent. Quamquam, etsi quaedam inter domesticos, ut ita dixerim, disserebant, non tamen ea fuisse credendum est quae aliam regulam fidei superducerent, diversam et contrariam illi quam catholice in medium proferebant, ut alium deum in ecclesia dicerent, alium in hospitio, aliam Christi substantiam designarent in aperto, aliam in secreto, aliam spem resurrectionis apud omnes annuntiarent, aliam apud paucos, cum ipsi obsecrarent in epistulis suis, ut id ipsum et unum loquerentur omnes, et non essent schismata et dissensiones in ecclesia, quia sive Paulus sive alii eadem praedicarent. Alioquin meminerant, Sit sermo vester: est, est, non, non, nam quod amplius, hoc a malo est, ne evangelium in diversitate tractarent.
thought_title: The apostles preached openly, not in secret
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that the apostles did not keep any hidden doctrine back from the churches, since the Lord commanded open proclamation.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover it was a consequence that, to the one to whom he was entrusting the administration of the gospel, not to be administered indiscriminately nor without consideration, he should add according to the Lord's saying, that he should not throw a pearl to pigs and a holy thing to dogs. The Lord said openly, without any indication of some hidden sacrament. He himself had commanded that, if they had heard anything in darkness and in secret, they should preach it in the light and on the housetops. He himself had prefigured by a parable that they should not keep one mina, that is one word of his, without fruit in a hidden place. He himself taught that a lamp is not usually hidden under a bushel, but is placed on a lampstand, so that it may shine for all who are in the house. The apostles either neglected these things or understood them very little, if they did not fulfill them, hiding something of the Light, that is of the word of God and the sacrament of Christ. They feared no one, as far as I know, not the violence of the Jews, not that of the Gentiles; all the more certainly they preached freely in the church, who were not silent in synagogues and in public places. Indeed they could neither have converted the Jews nor brought in the Gentiles, unless they set forth in order what they wanted to be believed by them. Much more, to churches already believing, they would have withdrawn nothing that they might entrust separately to a few others. Although, even if they discussed certain things among household members, so to speak, it is not to be believed that those things were such as to introduce another rule of faith, different and contrary to that one which they brought forth publicly in the catholic manner, so that they proclaimed one god in the church, another in private lodging, indicated one substance of Christ in the open, another in secret, announced one hope of resurrection among all, another among a few, since they themselves begged in their letters that all should speak that same one thing, and that there should not be schisms and dissensions in the church, because whether Paul or the others preached the same things. Otherwise they remembered, Let your speech be: yes, yes, no, no, for what is more than this is from evil, so that they would not treat the gospel in diversity.

choices.why: Keeps the legal/managerial force of administratio, matching the argument about how the gospel is to be handled.
Neuter singular substantive, matching the parallel with 'pearl' as a thing not to be thrown.
Literal rendering of the flat roofs used for public proclamation in the ancient world.
The glossary context uses 'Gentiles' for non-Jews; ethnicus is the standard term.
Adverb preserving the sense of universal, public, common proclamation, not a denominational label.
Hospitium means a private residence or lodging, contrasting with the public church assembly.

pass_b_english: It followed, then, that when he entrusted the administration of the gospel to someone, since it was not to be administered carelessly or at random, he added, in keeping with the Lord's own words, that he should not throw a pearl to pigs or a holy thing to dogs (Matthew 7:6). The Lord said this openly, without any hint of some hidden mystery. He himself had commanded that whatever they heard in darkness and in secret they should proclaim in the light and on the housetops (Matthew 10:27). He himself had prefigured through a parable that they should not keep a single mina, that is, a single word of his, stored away in hiding without fruit (Luke 19:20). He himself taught that a lamp is not usually hidden under a bushel, but placed on a lampstand so that it gives light to everyone in the house (Matthew 5:15).

The apostles either neglected these instructions or understood them very poorly, if they failed to carry them out by hiding something of the Light, that is, of the word of God and the mystery of Christ. They feared no one, as far as I know: not the violence of the Jews, not that of the Gentiles. All the more, then, they surely preached freely in the church, since they did not keep silent in synagogues and public places. Indeed, they could not have converted Jews or brought in Gentiles unless they set forth in an orderly way what they wanted them to believe. Much less would they have withheld anything from churches that already believed, to entrust it separately to a few others.

And yet, even if they did discuss certain matters among the household, so to speak, it must not be believed that these were things that would introduce another rule of faith, different from and contrary to the one they proclaimed publicly in the catholic manner. As if they declared one God in the church and another in private lodging, presented one substance of Christ in the open and another in secret, announced one hope of resurrection to everyone and another to a few. For they themselves pleaded in their letters that everyone should speak the same thing and one thing, and that there should be no schisms and dissensions in the church, because whether Paul or the others, they preached the same things (1 Corinthians 1:10). Otherwise they would have remembered: "Let your speech be: yes, yes, no, no; for anything more than this is from evil" (Matthew 5:37), so that they would not handle the gospel in divergent ways.

fixed: The source reads 'ut cui demandabat evangelii administrationem non passim nec inconsiderate administrandam, adiceret' — 'to the one to whom he was entrusting the administration of the gospel, not to be administered indiscriminately nor without consideration, he should add.' The English repeats the clause 'to the one to whom he entrusted the administration of the gospel' twice, which is redundant and not in the source. Removing the second occurrence fixes the circular repetition while preserving the meaning.
